significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that element-embedding geometry across crystal graph networks and composition transformers forms a "two-to-three-dimensional manifold recovering group/period," with independently tabulated electronegativity and atomic size aligned to its axes and residual structure exceeding a co-occurrence baseline; it also adds a narrower form-(ii) claim through the "causal swap." This establishes a definite representational phenomenon and some causal influence on formation-energy or band-gap predictions, constraining interpretations of whether model chemistry reflects atomic-property relationships rather than corpus frequency, although it does not provide a broader scientific law of material behavior; Atom2Vec (Zhou et al., PNAS 2018) illustrates why the physical interpretation of learned element geometry is relevant to downstream materials modeling. The negative branch would meaningfully reject the strong rediscovery account in favor of co-occurrence or model-specific organization, and true versus false are distinguishable despite "align" lacking a numerical threshold. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic alone would not earn this score, but recovering established scientific structure from embeddings is still the obvious first hypothesis for this topic, so the added dimensionality, confound dissociation, and causal consequence raise it only modestly above the median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "group-neighborhood consistency score," low-dimensional property-aligned axes, and an embedding-substitution intervention that tests whether predictions "shift toward the neighbor's true values." These are principally post-hoc diagnostics and analysis interventions rather than ex-ante screens: the claim suggests relevance to extrapolation but does not assert that the score forecasts an under-sampled-chemistry failure before prediction or deployment. After re-extraction on a new model, the conclusion does predict a transferable relation—"two-to-three-dimensional" organization by group/period with axes aligned to electronegativity and size—rather than merely prescribing another search, and its asserted scope covers both "crystal graph networks and composition transformers"; likely downstream users are materials-model researchers and auditors rather than experimental scientists or deployment decision-makers. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score because the topic alone supplies neither these diagnostics nor the transferable geometric relation, supporting reach above the topic median but not the practitioner-facing or ex-ante reach required for the highest bands.
